turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
I came in because I just can't stop thinking about my face. The left side of it just looks off. My nose and my jaw are crooked, and it's really obvious in every ID photo or whenever I have my camera on for my online classes. 

People tell me they don't see it when I bring it up, but... I know it's there. I feel like everyone in the CNC lab is noticing it before they even look at my work. It's just constantly on my mind and I don't know how to stop focusing on it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes a constant preoccupation with perceived flaws in their face (crooked nose and jaw) that others say they do not see, which is characteristic of preoccupation with appearance.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself spending a lot of time repeatedly checking your face in mirrors or other reflective surfaces throughout the day?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. Especially before I leave for school. I get... stuck, I guess, just checking my face in the bathroom mirror. And then I'll pull up my phone camera to check it there, too. I spend a lot of time trying to fix my hair or changing my shirt, just trying to find a way to hide the angle of my jaw. 

I keep asking my mom if it looks weird, too. Honestly, sometimes I do all this for so long that I end up missing my lab completely. Or if I do finally make it in, I show up so wiped out from stressing over it that I can't even focus on my work.

symptom_reasoning.S059: The patient states that they get so stressed and wiped out that they cannot focus on their work.
symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient expresses concern over the appearance of their jaw, trying to hide its angle and worrying that it looks weird.
symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient describes repetitive behaviors such as checking mirrors and phone cameras, changing clothes to camouflage their appearance, and seeking reassurance from their mother.

turns.doctor_question: Deep down, do you ever feel that your face might actually look completely normal and that your mind could be exaggerating it, or are you completely convinced it really is deformed?
turns.patient_response: I... I don't really know. I mean, I hear people when they tell me they don't see it, but I don't feel like my mind is making it up or exaggerating anything. When I look in the mirror or at a photo, it's just right there. I see it. So, yeah, I guess I'm pretty convinced it really is crooked. I don't see how it could just be in my head.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes being convinced that their face is crooked and seeing the defect in mirrors and photos, even though others tell them they do not see it.

turns.doctor_question: When you are around others, do you believe people are actually talking about, mocking, or reacting to your face, or is it more of a worry that they might notice it?
turns.patient_response: I think it's more of a worry. I don't really hear people whispering about me or anything like that, and no one has ever made fun of me to my face. It's just... I feel like they must be noticing it. Like when I'm in the lab, I just get this overwhelming feeling that they're looking at my jaw or my nose, even if they aren't saying anything. So, no, I don't think they're actively mocking me, I just worry a lot that they see how crooked it is.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes an overwhelming worry that others are noticing perceived flaws in their appearance, specifically their jaw and nose.
symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies having a fixed belief that people are actively mocking or talking about them, recognizing it instead as a worry.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing people whispering about them.
